summary: Torkel Brekke works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oslo under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson, and at Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He held positions at PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School of Theology.

Toru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held academic posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, including its Institute for Research in Humanities.

Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, where he served as professor, dean, and director, later directing the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute.

Toru Kumeji is a researcher in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held positions at the National Institute for Digital Humanities and as a chief researcher at the Institute of Humanities Information Studies.

Toru Sagara was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He later held academic posts at Ibaraki University, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoritsu Women's University.

Toru Takahashi was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Daegu Higher Common School, Keijo Imperial University, Dongguk University, Fukuoka University, and Tenri University.

Toru Tomabechi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, and has held posts at the University of Lausanne, the Institute of Humanities Information Studies, and the National Institute for Digital Humanities.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from around 1966 to 1975 and later held a post there from around 1980 to 2017.

Toshifumi Goto is a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, studying under Karl Hoffmann and others. He has held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University.
Toshihide Unebe is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Issai Funahashi and served as a professor at Doho University.

Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at Keio University. He held academic positions at Keio University, McGill University, and the Iranian Research Institute of Philosophy.
Toshihiko Kimura works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tohoku University, he held posts at Tohoku University, Tokai Gakuin University, and Shitennoji University.
Toshihiro Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an associate professor and later as a professor at Shuchiin University.
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha. He has held academic posts at Nagoya University.

Toshiichi Endo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate degree at the University of Kelaniya and his doctoral thesis at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, supervised by Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.

Toshikazu Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He has worked as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and was appointed professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Hokkaido University. He held posts as a professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature and at Kyoto University of the Arts.

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He has held positions at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, Kacho Junior College, and the Research Institute of Old Japanese Manuscripts of Buddhist Scriptures.
Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from around 1930 to 1934. He later held posts at Doho University and Otani University.

Toshio Horiuchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD at the University of Tokyo. He has held positions as a postdoctoral researcher at Zhejiang University and as a visiting researcher at Toyo University.
